findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in JavaScript i18next bundle
findings.body: This account-ui bundle and the corresponding admin-ui bundle use i18next interpolation, as shown by surrounding keys such as '{{0}}' and '{{name}}'. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' therefore will not be interpolated by the JavaScript UI; users will see literal placeholders/choice syntax instead of the attribute name and limits. The Java choice-format conversion is appropriate for the server-side theme bundles, but the js/apps account/admin bundles must retain their {{...}} interpolation (with pluralization expressed in an i18next-compatible way if needed).

findings.title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian (lt) account bundle now has totpStep1='Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian (the same Italian string was also put into the Lithuanian login bundle). Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the anchor tags should be removed from a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:' instead.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text put into Simplified Chinese bundle
findings.body: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) bundle now has totpStep1='在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', written in Traditional Chinese characters (手機/安裝/應用程式). Simplified Chinese users should get the Simplified rendering (e.g. 手机/安装/应用程序), consistent with the rest of this file.

findings.title: Verifier aborts with RuntimeException when no English counterpart exists
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by regex-rewriting the absolute path and throws an unchecked RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. verify() only catches IOException, so a single translated file without a resolvable *_en.properties counterpart (a newly added locale, or a bundle whose English source lives in a differently-named tree than the 'resources-community'->'resources' rewrite assumes) aborts the whole verification run with a stack trace instead of producing a per-file verification message or checking the remaining files.

findings.title: Any HTML in English enables all allowed tags in every translation
findings.body:
containsHtml() only tests whether the English value contains any tag, and then POLICY_SOME_HTML unconditionally allows br, p, strong and b in the translation. A translation of a key whose English text contains a single
(or only an anchor, which also satisfies HTML_TAGS) can therefore freely add

, and markup that never existed in the source, and it will pass verification. Only the anchor tags are compared against the English original in santizeAnchors(); the other allowed elements should likewise be restricted to those present in the English value if the goal is to prevent translators from introducing new HTML.

findings.title: Anchor check requires translations to keep English anchor order
findings.body: santizeAnchors() walks the translation's anchors and the English anchors in lockstep and reports 'Didn't find anchor tag' as soon as the next pair differs, then breaks. Legitimate translations, especially for languages with different word order, may reorder the same anchors relative to the English sentence; those will be falsely flagged (and, because the remaining anchors are left in the value, will typically also produce a second spurious 'Illegal HTML' message). The check should compare the multiset of anchor tags rather than their sequence, and its message also omits the key and file, unlike the Illegal HTML message, making failures hard to locate in large bundles.
